tagline: College streets, canal country, and the Harrison family.
intro: From Oxford, founded in 1810 as the home of Miami University, the drive runs south past Okeana on Dry Fork Creek toward Harrison and Cleves. It ends near North Bend, where William Henry Harrison made his home and his grandson Benjamin was born.

Harrison backed the canal that came through this country, selling land for its right-of-way and supplying wood and bricks for a tunnel through the ridge between North Bend and Cleves. Floods ended the canal in 1856. Trains used the tunnel until 1888, and it has since silted up almost to the ceiling.

moments.title: Oxford
moments.text: Freedom Summer began here in June 1964 with orientations at Western College for Women, an event commemorated near Kumler Chapel.

moments.title: Harrison
moments.text: Named for William Henry Harrison, the town was one of the few stops in Ohio on the Whitewater Canal.

moments.title: William Henry Harrison Tomb
moments.text: Harrison died a month into his presidency; his family buried him on the crest of Mt. Nebo, and his son John Scott, son of one president and father of another, shares the vault.
